title: When I need to migrate a phone number between BSPs or from on-premise API to Cloud API, I want a sea
target_user: Platform Engineer responsible for WhatsApp infrastructure
job_to_be_done: When I need to migrate a phone number between BSPs or from on-premise API to Cloud API, I want a seamless migration process with clear steps and minimal downtime, so I can switch vendors or upgrade infrastructure without losing messaging capability or number quality.
painful_workflow: Migrating a phone number between BSPs or from on-premise WhatsApp Business API to Cloud API. Requires manually disabling 2FA, re-verifying ownership, coordinating downtime, and reconfiguring webhooks.
current_workaround: Scheduled maintenance windows, running parallel test numbers, manual coordination with both old and new BSP, and support tickets when registration or 2FA reset fails.

competitors.name: Meta WhatsApp Business API Migration Guide
competitors.notes: Official documentation from Meta outlining steps to migrate numbers from on-premise to Cloud API or between BSPs. Not a tool – it's a manual guide. No automation or UI.
competitors.feature_overlap: Provides step-by-step instructions for disabling 2FA, re-verifying ownership, and reconfiguring webhooks. Overlaps with the problem description but requires manual execution.
competitors.market_positioning: Meta's official reference for migration; not a commercial product.

competitors.name: Twilio WhatsApp Number Migration Support
competitors.notes: Twilio offers support and documentation for migrating numbers to/from their platform. They provide a migration checklist and can assist via support tickets. Not a standalone tool.
competitors.feature_overlap: Covers the same workflow (disable 2FA, verify ownership, update webhooks) but relies on manual steps and Twilio support team involvement.
competitors.pricing: Included with Twilio WhatsApp API usage; no separate fee for migration support.
competitors.market_positioning: Part of Twilio's CPaaS offering; positions migration as a supported process, not a product.

competitors.name: MessageBird Number Porting
competitors.notes: MessageBird provides documentation and support for porting WhatsApp numbers. They have a dedicated migration team for complex cases. Still manual coordination.
competitors.feature_overlap: Same core steps; offers a migration form and support ticket system. No self-service automation.
competitors.pricing: Included with MessageBird WhatsApp API usage.
competitors.market_positioning: Value-added service for customers switching to/from MessageBird.

competitors.name: GitHub: whatsapp-number-migration-script
competitors.notes: Several open-source scripts exist that attempt to automate parts of the migration (e.g., resetting 2FA via API, updating webhooks). Quality varies, no official support, often outdated.
competitors.feature_overlap: Automates some API calls but lacks end-to-end orchestration, error handling, and zero-downtime guarantees.
competitors.market_positioning: Hobbyist or internal tooling; not a polished SaaS product.

competitors.name: WATI Migration Services
competitors.notes: WATI (a WhatsApp BSP) offers migration assistance for businesses moving to their platform. They handle the process manually with dedicated support.
competitors.feature_overlap: Covers the full migration workflow but is a service, not a self-service tool. Requires engaging WATI sales/support.
competitors.pricing: Free for WATI customers (included in onboarding).
competitors.market_positioning: Part of WATI's customer acquisition; not a standalone product.

substitutes.name: Manual scheduled maintenance with parallel test numbers
substitutes.notes: Common workaround: run a second number in parallel, test, then switch. No tooling, high operational overhead.
substitutes.feature_overlap: Achieves the same outcome (migration) but with downtime, manual steps, and risk of message loss.
substitutes.market_positioning: Default approach for most platform engineers today.

verified_facts: A forum post on Meta's developer community describes phone number migration between BSPs or from on-premise to Cloud API as problematic (SIG-003).
The post mentions numbers getting stuck between states and registration failures (SIG-003).
inferences: The problem likely occurs during the migration process, not as a daily operational issue.
The user is a platform engineer or developer managing WhatsApp infrastructure.
The workaround involves manual coordination and support tickets, suggesting no automated solution exists.
assumptions: The single forum post represents a broader, unexpressed pain (not verified).
The problem is severe enough to warrant a paid SaaS solution (not verified).
Users would pay for a tool that automates migration (not verified).
The migration frequency is high enough to justify a subscription (not verified).
unknowns: How many businesses experience this problem?
What is the actual downtime or revenue loss per migration failure?
Are there existing tools or services that partially solve this?
What is the typical frequency of phone number migrations per business?
Are users actively seeking or paying for a solution?
Is this problem specific to certain BSPs or regions?
What is the success rate of the current manual workaround?
rejection_reasons: Judge rejected: Deterministic hard gates are not met: pain, frequency, and willingness to pay are all scored 2/5, far below the required threshold of 4 for approval. Evidence is also critically thin (1 independent source, 1 source type), and both the bear case (confidence 0.85) and customer perspective (confidence 0.85) independently conclude that free BSP-provided migration support and Meta’s documentation make a paid, dedicated tool unlikely to gain traction or monetize.
